evidence.quote: The five of you are, in this moment, standing in… something that's darker than blackness, having just passed through the door into the prison.

Surrounding a central prison chamber, the Order built the house as a magical and mechanical device to untether the central prison room from the world around it and to keep the physical and the temporal location of that central room constantly changing. If it stopped moving somehow, the prisoner would quickly escape.

p02.label: House of 27 Rooms

evidence.quote: DM: Joined by Menestheus, a member of Thalestria's party who she left behind when she made the bargain, the group enters the house of 27 rooms.

p02.note: The enclosing complex is the 27th House. The central prison chamber remains a distinct place; the transcript sometimes uses “27th room” for the whole powered complex.

evidence.quote: Oh, it's so funny. This is in my notes that I read over before every session, but I never actually said, like, so the Twilight Kingdoms… where you were, are one of the interstitial spaces where, rather than, like, a big lord ruling all of it…

relations.note: The debrief identifies the realm in which this adventure’s houses stand; it does not give the moving chamber a fixed physical or temporal coordinate.

p04.label: Root opening inside the prison

evidence.quote: DM: Yes. In the corner off… sort of to your right, as you're still sort of standing by the entrance. There is… you know, you go a foot or two in, and then realizing where you are back, back out again.

DM: A hollow, root-like structure that seems to you almost identical to the one which you crawled from the, from Taelgar to the Feywild through. A room that's… at least by its, sort of, dimensions and size and shape, suggests that it's grown out of the prison.

p04.note: Txarro briefly probes the opening and backs out. Its resemblance to the original portal and the discussion of its 1351 exit do not establish the party’s arrival beyond it.

p05.label: Hillside above the ravine

evidence.quote: And the ruins and remains of the prison and of the house, now shaken apart around you as you were sheltered under one of these horror leaves, are sliding down the sides of the cliff, and into the ravine, and into the darkness.
DM: And the five of you are left on an empty hillside, in the gathering twilight just as the first stars of evening are beginning to come out.

p05.note: The promontory, former doorframe, ravine, and surviving well identify Twilight Promontory; the name itself is verified in the vault note, while this session calls it a hillside or promontory (u2526–u2527).

p06.label: Low stone well

evidence.quote: The child is sitting at the edge of a low stone well, maybe a foot high above the cliffside where a doorframe used to be leading into the house.

p06.note: The child descends; the travelers do not. Earlier stories describe its home at the bottom of the bottomless well.

evidence.quote: The child is sitting at the edge of a low stone well, maybe a foot high above the cliffside where a doorframe used to be leading into the house.

p07.label: Old house at the edge of Tellim

evidence.quote: DM: And it's the last of the sunset shining through a high window of an old house onto the bloody and exhausted form of Lord Hulda. Surrounded by the butchered corpse of the half-dozen mushroom men Aldens, who were his servants. And he drinks a potion, but his wounds don't fully close, and he coughs, and then he coughs again, and he doesn't stop coughing until he does, all at once.

p07.note: Hulda and his fungal servants identify the Material Plane Dandelion House, distinct from the Feywild 27th House. The debrief separately confirms Dandelion House’s destruction at u2521–u2522.

p08.label: Woods at the wild edges of Tellim

evidence.quote: DM: Below the old trees, on the wild edges of the Duchy of Tellim, it's always dusk. And in that twilight, the pale mushroom children of the Thirst walk without sleeping or dreaming or hungering, and they flee from fire and iron, and they make new siblings out of anyone they find. And they search in those woods, always, obsessively, for the hidden door that will bring them back home to their parent again.

p08.note: The source describes continuing fungal children in these woods. Dandelion House’s vault note identifies Varrow Forest as its modern locality; this source does not speak the forest name or define its boundaries.

evidence.quote: In a room filled with glass tanks of fungus growing on severed limbs, just as you feel the first rumbles start to vibrate through it, just as you can see the glass tanks shaking and the house is destroyed, a body in the shape of a dwarven woman, but made from fungi and lichens of every possible description, sits up and looks, for a long moment, at the lifeless corpse which once held the soul now encased in its own fungal golem flesh.

DM: And as the room around her shakes, as pieces of the ceiling begin to fall to the floor, Kallipseis, now wizard head of Arithrimos Lamperum in a golem body, consults a book filled with long lists of six-digit numbers and blinks out of sight.

p10.label: Thatched cottage beside the sunset road

evidence.quote: DM: Camera pulls back, and it's a quiet, thatched cottage by the side of a road which runs parallel exactly to the sunset, and a tigerman is stowing in his bag the polished sphere of crystal through which he watched a golem plane shift out of the Feywild.

p10.note: Rakshasa’s epilogue location, distinct from the party’s physical position. Its exact larger locality is not supplied by this passage.

p11.label: Black nothingness beyond the universe

evidence.quote: DM: It is no time. It is not time, it is outside of time, in the black nothingness beyond the universe, where the black stars do not shine, and an un-thing that is sometimes a child, and sometimes a monster can once again see the complete and unambiguous shape of all of its own possibilities. Its past, its present, its future, all at once, unhidden, always moving, never changing.

p11.note: The destination is explicitly outside time and the universe. The source does not identify one named Far Realm or provide ordinary spatial coordinates.

p12.label: Lord of the Ended Revel’s manor

evidence.quote: DM: Under a twilight sky, wide green lawns rise from the river to a beautiful manor house where a party has finished. The paper lanterns hanging on long lines are all extinguished, and the grounds are silent, and the partygoers have departed.

DM: And in the upper room of the dark house, the Lord of the Ended Revel looks out a high window toward the place where the sun has set, thinking of the child he befriended just before his party began.

p12.note: The same estate remains after the party ends; its new session-era name is confirmed at u2523–u2524.
